title: Orthogonal interventions are required to identify split androgen-response branches

known_answers.result: A_AR and M effects are not separately identifiable

known_answers.interpretation: more doses along the same branch direction
known_answers.result: additional same-direction perturbations do not solve branch confounding

known_answers.interpretation: DHT challenge + AR-specific block + mechanical relaxation
known_answers.result: the two branch coefficients are locally identifiable inside the frozen linear model

biological_motivation.source: Li et al., Nature Communications 2026, doi:10.1038/s41467-026-70153-4
observations: DHT increased DS/CTS contractility and impaired human hair-follicle growth
AR knockdown alleviated part of DHT-associated growth inhibition but did not alter CTS contraction
GPR133 knockdown or ML-7 reduced the contractile branch and rescued major pathological phenotypes
PIEZO1 activation phenocopied growth retardation and progenitor injury while PIEZO1 inhibition rescued MCH-associated phenotypes

claim_boundary: rank 2 is a design property, not proof that real interventions are perfectly selective
the local linear output model is a synthetic approximation
off-target effects, incomplete blockade, nonlinear coupling and donor heterogeneity can still break parameter recovery
this does not establish clinical benefit or recommend any intervention
next_test: Use source-level or prospective paired perturbation data to estimate cross-talk and test whether the nominal AR and mechanical probes remain sufficiently non-collinear in real human follicle systems.
